Rashi on Eruvin 30a:10:1.hebrew: באומר כל הזן עלי - מתני' דאסר ליה בכל מילי, לאו דאמר "יאסר עלי מזון", דודאי לא מיקרי מזון אלא ה' מינין דהוו מין דגן, דזייני וסעדי ליבא; אלא כגון דאמר "יאסר עלי כל הזן", דמשמע כל דבר המשביע — דכל מילי זייני, חוץ ממים ומלח; אבל מיסעד לא סעדי, ולא מיקרו מזון:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:10:1.english: In [a case of one] who says: "Anything that nourishes [is forbidden] to me" - [As for] the Mishnah, which forbade him from all things, it is not [a case where] he said, "May sustenance [mazon] be forbidden to me," for certainly nothing is called mazon except the five species that are kinds of grain, which nourish and sustain the heart; rather, [it is a case] such as where he said, "May anything that nourishes be forbidden to me," which means anything that satisfies [hunger]. For all things nourish, except for water and salt; but they do not sustain [the heart], and [therefore] they are not called mazon.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:11:1.hebrew: גינוסר - ארץ ים כינרת, ופירותיה מתוקין:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:11:1.english: Ginosar - The land of the Sea of Galilee, and its fruits are sweet.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:11:2.hebrew: דלא טעים לי זיונא - לא אכלתי לשובע, ועדיין אני רעב:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:11:2.english: That I have not tasted something that nourishes - I have not eaten to satiety, and I am still hungry.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:11:3.hebrew: זיונא ס"ד - לא גרסינן הכא, אלא במס' ברכות; והכא גרסינן: אימא מזונא:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:11:3.english: "[Something that] nourishes" — could [that] enter your mind? - We do not read [this] here, but rather in Tractate Berakhot; and here we read: "Say: Sustaining food."

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:12:1.hebrew: מערבין לו בה - דלא נדר אלא מאכילה. ואי משום דלא חזיא ליה — הא חזיא לאחריני, מידי דהוה אנזיר ביין:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:12:1.english: One may establish an eiruv for him with it - For he only vowed against eating [it]. And if [you say] because it is not fit for him — behold, it is fit for others, just as in [the case of] a nazirite with wine.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:12:2.english: “This loaf [is forbidden] to me” - This implies that he is prohibiting any form of benefit from it to himself.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:13:1.hebrew: מאי לאו דאמר עלי - ושמע מינה, דלא אסר איניש אדעתיה אלא דרך עיקר הנאתה, וכי נדר — אדעתא דאכילה נדר:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:13:1.english: What, is it not [referring to a case] where he said, “[It is forbidden] to me”? - And infer from this that a person does not intend to forbid [anything] other than in the manner of its primary benefit, and when he vowed, he vowed with eating in mind.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:13:2.english: No, where he said: "Behold, this" - [He said:] "[I take an] oath that I will not eat this loaf."

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:15:1.hebrew: הקדש - ודאי אסר בכל הנאות, ואינו ראוי לשום אדם:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:15:1.english: Consecrated - It is certainly forbidden for all forms of benefit, and is not fit for any person.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:15:2.english: In itself - In an unconsecrated loaf.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:16:1.english: Rather, what? Wherever one said “[forbidden] to me,” one may establish an eiruv - For [that expression] implies only eating.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:16:2.hebrew: קשיא רישא - דקתני: ״אימתי? בזמן שאמר שבועה שלא אטעמנה״, דמשמע: הא אמר ״עלי״ — לא. ומשני: הא לא קשיא, ד״חסורי מיחסרא כו' עד נעשה כאומר כו'״ — דלא מסיק אדעתיה לאסור עליו אלא דרך הנאתה, דהיינו אכילה:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:16:2.english: There is a difficulty from the first clause - For it teaches: "When? At the time that he said: 'I swear that I shall not taste it,'" which implies: but if he said: "[This loaf is forbidden] to me," no, [one may not establish an eiruv for him with it]. And [the Gemara] answers: This is not difficult, as [the baraita] "is incomplete, etc.," until: "it is as though he said, etc." — for it did not enter his mind to forbid [it] to himself except in the manner of its [customary] benefit, which is eating.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:19:1.hebrew: אדם אוסר עצמו באוכל - שתלה הנדר במעשה שהוא עושה בעצמו, דהיינו שלא אוכל:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:19:1.english: A person prohibits himself from food - That he made the vow dependent on an action that he performs himself, namely: "That I will not eat."

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:19:2.hebrew: מערבין לו בה - דהא הנאה דממילא היא, ולאו איהו עביד:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:19:2.english: One may establish an eiruv for him with it - For this is a benefit that comes on its own, and he is not performing [an action].

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:19:3.hebrew: אוכל הנאסר על האדם - כגון: "ככר זו תיאסר עלי", או: "שבועה שלא אהנה מככר זו" — דהשתא לא תלה האיסור במעשה שבגופו, אלא אפילו הנאה דממילא — אין מערבין לו בה. ל"א: "ככר זו עלי" — מערבין לו בה, דאמר לקמן (עירובין דף לא.): אין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה, ומצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו; הלכך, משום הנאה לא איכפת לן. ואי משום דלא חזיא ליה — הא חזיא לאחרים, דומיא דנזיר ביין. "ככר זו הקדש" — לא חזיא לא לדידיה ולא לאחריני, ואנן סעודה הראויה בעינן, כדלקמן. זה עיקר:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:19:3.english: Food that is prohibited to a person - For example: "This loaf shall be forbidden to me," or: "[I take an] oath that I will not derive benefit from this loaf." For in this case, he did not condition the prohibition on an action of his [own] body, but rather [prohibited] even passive benefit; [therefore,] one may not establish an eiruv for him with it. Another explanation: "[If one said:] This loaf [is forbidden] to me, one may establish an eiruv for him with it" — for [the Gemara] states below (Eruvin 31a): One may establish an eiruv only for the purpose of a mitzvah, and mitzvot were not given for [personal] benefit; therefore, regarding benefit, we do not care. And if [you say that one cannot establish an eiruv with it] because it is not fit for him — behold, it is fit for others, similar to a nazir with wine. "[Whereas if he said:] This loaf is consecrated" — it is not fit either for him or for others, and we require a fit meal, as [explained] below. This is the primary [explanation].

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג אבל בגדי עשירים לעניים לא - כלומר, לעניים לא בעינן בגדי עשירים, אלא כיון דלדידהו חזו — אזלי בתרייהו. הכא נמי, אע"ג דלפרסאי לאו ליפתן הוא, כיון דלדידן הוי ליפתן — ניסגי בשיעור זוטא:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:1:1.english: This is the reading: “But the clothing of the wealthy for the poor, no” - That is to say, for the poor we do not require [the standard of] the clothing of the wealthy; rather, since it is usable for them, we follow their [standard]. Here too, even though for the Persians it is not a relish, since for us it is a relish, let it suffice with the smaller measure.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:2:1.hebrew: הכא לחומרא - דכיון דחזו להו, מקבלי טומאה:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:2:1.english: Here [it is] for stringency - For since they are fit for them, they are susceptible to ritual impurity:

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:2:2.hebrew: והכא לחומרא - דעד דהוי ליפתן לכ"ע, ליבעי שיעורא רבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:2:2.english: And here [it is] for stringency - That unless it is a relish for everyone, it should require the larger measure.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:2:3.hebrew: והתניא - גבי עירוב: דכיון דחזו לזקן ולחולה, אף על גב דלכל אדם לא הוי מזון שתי סעודות, מערבין מיהא למאן דחזי; וגבי רעבתן דאכיל טפי, סגי בבינונית. אלמא לקולא אזלינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:2:3.english: Wasn’t it taught - With regard to an *eiruv*: Since it is fit for an elderly person and for an ill person, even though for any [other] person it would not be [enough] food for two meals, one may nevertheless establish an *eiruv* for the one for whom it is fit; and with regard to a glutton who eats more, an average [meal] suffices. Evidently, we follow leniency.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:3:1.hebrew: פתחו כמלואו - להציל על שאר פתחים, ואי ליכא פתח דחזי ליה — כל חור מלא אגרוף שבכתלים טמאין:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:3:1.english: His opening [must be] his full size - To save the other openings [from impurity]; and if there is no opening suitable for him, every fist-sized hole in the walls is impure.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:4:1.english: Should we cut it into pieces - [Should] they cut it into limbs?

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:5:1.english: Do the Rabbis disagree - Regarding [the case of] a corpse in a house.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:6:2.hebrew: בההוא מרווח - הלכך מציל על כולן. אבל כולן שוין, בד' או בי' אמות — כולן טמאין, דלא ידעי בהי מרווח ומפיק. ואפילו נפתח אחד מהן והאחרים סגורין, או חישב עליו להוציאו באחד מהן — דתנן בגמרא במסכת ביצה (דף לז:): "הוא טמא וכולן טהורים" — ה"מ היכי דהאי חזי ליה, ואפילו כולהו חזי ליה; אבל היכא דליכא חד חזי ליה, ובעי מרווח, וכולן שוין — לא ידעינן בהי מרווח:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:6:2.english: In that [one] he will widen - Therefore, it protects all [the other openings]. However, [if] they are all equal — [whether] of four or of ten cubits — they are all impure, for we do not know in which [one] he will widen and take [the corpse] out. And even [if] one of them was opened and the others were closed, or he intended to take it out through one of them — as we learned in the Gemara in Tractate Beitzah (37b): "[That one] is impure and all [the others] are pure" — this applies only where this [opening] is suitable for it, even [if] all of them are suitable for it; but where there is not even one [opening that] is suitable for it, and it requires widening, and they are all equal — we do not know in which [one] he will widen.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:7:1.hebrew: סיני - קרי רב יוסף, לפי שהיה בקי במשניות ובברייתות:
Rashi on Eruvin 30a:7:1.english: Sinai - He calls Rav Yosef [Sinai], because he was well-versed in Mishnayot and Baraitot.

Rashi on Eruvin 30a:9:1.english: And did we not refute him on one occasion - In [the chapter] Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 35b).

Tosafot on Eruvin 30a:12:1.hebrew: ככר זו עלי אין מערבין לו בה - תימה לר"י: אמאי נקט בהאי שבועה ובהאי נדר? בשבועה גופה או בנדר גופיה הוה מצי לפלוגי, דהיכא דאסר עליה באכילה — מערבין לו בה, בהנאה — אין מערבין לו בה! ועוד, דאמר לקמן (עירובין דף לא.): לכ"ע אין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה, ומצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו — משמע דליכא תנא דפליג; והא רבי אליעזר דבסמוך, דאמר "ככר זו עלי" דאין מערבין לו בה משום דאסור בהנאה — אם כן, סבר דמערבין לו לדבר הרשות, או מצות ליהנות ניתנו! ונראה כרשב"ם, דמפרש דאין מערבין לו בה אפי' אמר "קונם אכילת ככר זו עלי", משום דקונם הוי כעין הקדש, ואתי לאחלופי בהקדש; אבל אמר שבועה, אפילו אמר "שבועה שלא אהנה מככר זו", כיון דלא מיחלף בהקדש — מערבין לו בה, דאין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה, ומצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו; ונקט "שבועה שלא אוכל", דאפי' הכי בקונם אין מערבין לו בה. וקשה לפירושו: דכי פריך בסמוך לרב הונא "ליפלוג וליתני בדידיה", לישני דהכי קאמר: אבל אמר "עלי", נעשה כאומר "ככר זו הקדש", ואין מערבין לו בה! ולפי' הקונטרס ניחא, דאין לו לתלות בהקדשות, דאסירי לדידיה ולאחריני. ויש לומר, דלא מצי לשנויי הכי משום דמסיים בה "לפי שאין מערבין בהקדשות", משמע: דווקא בהקדשות, אבל בקונמות מערבין:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30a:12:1.english: "This loaf is upon me, one may not establish an eiruv for him with it" - The Ri finds it astonishing: Why did [Rav] formulate this [first case] as an oath and that [second case] as a vow? Within an oath itself or within a vow itself, he could have made the distinction: that where one forbade [it] to himself with respect to eating, one may establish an eiruv for him with it; [where he forbade it] with respect to benefit, one may not establish an eiruv for him with it! And furthermore, as [the Gemara] says below (Eruvin 31a): According to all, one may establish an eiruv only for the purpose of a mitzvah, and mitzvot were not given for benefit — which implies that there is no Tanna who disagrees; yet behold, Rabbi Eliezer nearby, who said that [if one said,] "This loaf is upon me," one may not establish an eiruv for him with it because it is forbidden in benefit — if so, he holds that one may establish an eiruv for a voluntary matter, or that mitzvot were given for benefit! And it appears in accordance with the Rashbam, who explains that one may not establish an eiruv for him with it even if he said "Konam the eating of this loaf upon me," because a konam is like a form of consecration, and people might come to confuse it with consecrated property; but if he took an oath, even if he said "I swear that I shall not derive benefit from this loaf," since it will not be confused with consecrated property, one may establish an eiruv for him with it, because one may establish an eiruv only for the purpose of a mitzvah, and mitzvot were not given for benefit. And [Rav] formulated [the oath as] "I swear that I shall not eat" [to indicate] that even so, in the case of a konam one may not establish an eiruv for him with it. And [yet] there is a difficulty according to his explanation: For when [the Gemara] challenges Rav Huna nearby, "Let him make a distinction and teach within [the case] itself," let [the Gemara] answer that this is what [the baraita] means: "However, if he said 'upon me,' he becomes like one who says 'This loaf is consecrated,' and one may not establish an eiruv for him with it!" And according to Rashi's explanation it is well understood, for [the baraita] should not link it to consecrated items, which are forbidden to him and to others. And one can say [in defense of the Rashbam] that [the Gemara] could not answer this way because [the baraita] concludes: "Because one may not establish an eiruv with consecrated items," which implies: specifically with consecrated items, but with konamot one may establish an eiruv.

Tosafot on Eruvin 30a:8:1.hebrew: לימא תהוי תיובתא - ואם תאמר: והא מאן דפליג ארב ושמואל לא פליג אלא באורז ודוחן, וא"כ תקשה לכולהו! ועוד, תיקשי ליה מתניתין דכיצד מברכין (ברכות דף מ:), דיש כמה דברים דמברכין עליו "שהכל" או בפ"ה! וי"ל: דדווקא לרב ושמואל פריך, דלא חשיבי אורז ודוחן אף על גב דקבעי נמי סעודתא עלייהו; א"כ סבירא להו דכל מילי לא מיקרו מזון אלא ה' מינין בלבד. אבל מאן דפליג עלייהו, סבר שפיר דכל מילי איקרו מזון, אך דלא תקנו "בורא מיני מזונות" אלא הך דקבעי סעודתא עלייהו, ואאורז ודוחן קבעי נמי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 30a:8:1.english: Let us say that this is a refutation - And if you say: But whoever disagrees with Rav and Shmuel only disagrees regarding rice and millet, and if so, it should present a difficulty to all of them! And furthermore, the Mishnah of Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 40b) should present a difficulty to him, as there are many items over which one recites shehakol or borei peri ha'eitz! And one can say: [The Gemara] poses the challenge specifically against Rav and Shmuel, because they do not consider rice and millet [as nourishment] even though one also establishes a meal upon them; if so, they hold that no items are called nourishment except for the five species alone. But whoever disagrees with them may well hold that all items are called nourishment, but [the Sages] only instituted [the blessing] "Borei minei mezonot" over that upon which one establishes a meal, and upon rice and millet one also establishes [a meal].
